title: Capture the Zoning Resolution sections the community-facility options need (Article II Chapter 4 and the Use Group III permission 22-13): documents only, source-text snapshots in the existing shape with byte-identical bundled copies. No rule, no reading of the text for any lot, no computed figure.
objective: Capture, from the official NYC DCP Zoning Resolution portal, the community-facility sections the options library marks NOT CAPTURED (DB-253; docs/zoning-law-library/options/option-06-07-community-facility.md): Article II Chapter 4 24-04, 24-11, 24-111, 24-161, 24-162, 24-163, 24-33, 24-34, 24-35, 24-36, 24-391, 24-52, 24-522, 24-56 and Article II Chapter 2 22-13 (the parent section only; its child sections, if the site has them, are listed in the producer report for a later capture). Each capture is one JSON file in the existing zr_section_snapshot/v1 shape (templates: docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/zr-23-344.snapshot.json and the eleven captures of M3-T008, e.g. zr-27-16.snapshot.json): HTML node request plus the print/PDF entityprint cross-check, sha256-pinned both channels (or the documented fallback, disclosed), the page's own Last Amended stamp, verbatim_excerpt with #term# markers and the list letters as the official PRINT shows them (the HTML markup can restart a list: M3-T008's G1 finding), content_digest_sha256 = sha256(verbatim_excerpt), extraction_status extracted_draft, raw_html_verified false, the ADR-007 not-professionally-reviewed label. Each lands in docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/ AND as a byte-identical copy in services/api/app/_zr_snapshots/v1/ produced by services/api/scripts/sync_zr_snapshots.py. A listed section whose node does not exist under the current text is reported, never invented. Documents only: no rule file, no reading of the text for any lot, no derived or computed number, no eligibility determination.
business_reason: The master plan lists options 2 to 11 as not planned because the law each still lacks is unread or not captured. The library's second pass (M3-T007; reviewed, G1 PASS) read these sections on the official site and left them not captured (backlog DB-243 and DB-253). A rule may cite a section only once it is captured with provenance (CLAUDE.md principles 2, 3 and 12). The affordable- and senior-housing subset was captured by M3-T008 (accepted); this task supplies the community-facility subset (options 6 and 7); the remaining subsets (split lot and courts; rooming units, shops and parking) follow as their own tasks, one at a time, so the official site is never loaded by several capture runs at once.

acceptance_scenarios.then: the file is in the zr_section_snapshot/v1 shape, content_digest_sha256 == sha256(verbatim_excerpt), it names its channel and is sha256-pinned on both channels (or records the documented 504/403 fallback), and SnapshotStore().load() loads it without error

acceptance_scenarios.when: python services/api/scripts/sync_zr_snapshots.py --check runs and tests/rules/test_zr_snapshot_bundle.py runs
acceptance_scenarios.then: --check exits 0 and every test passes: each bundled copy is byte-identical to its canonical source and membership matches
it stays green; each capture's request_url is the official article/chapter/section (or term) page, and no new section is cited by the benchmark fixture so no href changes

acceptance_scenarios.given: a listed section whose node does not exist under the current text, or whose official title or number differs from the library's list
acceptance_scenarios.when: it is looked up on the official site
acceptance_scenarios.then: it is reported in the producer report with the URL, the time and what the site shows; no file is written for a missing node and no text or title is invented

acceptance_scenarios.when: it is searched for status words
acceptance_scenarios.then: extraction_status is extracted_draft, raw_html_verified is false, nothing is labelled Verified, no rule / reading for a lot / derived or computed number / eligibility determination appears; section id, title, official URL and Last Amended date are taken from the official page read for this pass, not from memory
it touches only the allowed paths; no library doc, evidence record, rule, scenario, drawing or test file changes; each cited passage is the section's own verbatim source text

acceptance_scenarios.given: a captured section with lettered or numbered lists
acceptance_scenarios.when: its excerpt is compared with the official print/PDF
acceptance_scenarios.then: the list letters and numbers are the print's (one continuous list where the print has one), every word verbatim; where the print is unavailable the markup positions are disclosed with "cite by words"

risks: The ZR print/PDF big pages 504 and per-term print/PDF can 403 (DB-167): use the documented fallback (direct HTML GET, browser UA, sha256-pinned) and disclose it in cross_check/notes; never evade.
The 2024 City of Yes amendments renumbered sections: take every section number, title and Last Amended date from the official page read for this pass.
A capture changes no result, rule or label; a later rule task works its own independent example before any result changes (D-093).
A capture run loads the official site: one capture task runs at a time; the builder fetches only the pages it captures (two channels per section), with pauses, and stops on repeated refusals.
The HTML <ol> markup can restart a list's letters where the official print runs one list (M3-T008 G1 F1): take the letters from the print/PDF.
path_notes: Lane A (engine snapshots): docs/research/zr-snapshots/** and services/api/app/_zr_snapshots/** are Lane A; the producer report is Lane C. Run on a task/ branch so the lane-branch path check is skipped (a lane-a/ branch would reject the Lane-C report). Disjoint snapshot filenames from any sibling capture task, so A/B/C may run in parallel in separate worktrees. sync_zr_snapshots.py is RUN, never edited.

progress_log.message: claimed; one capture task at a time, so the official site is never loaded by several runs
